title: What spells "no cap" on the query length, instead of 0?
body:
The number 0 stands for "no cap" in four places at 1b1ecd0, and each reads it its own way. There were five when this issue was opened. b3f9104 removed the builder's cap and the cap in `find_lcp` and `merge_sort`, which were two of them. The differing readings caused sufr-106d02: `searched_len` took a caller's 0 as "compare the whole query" while `load_suffixes`, a function that is gone now, took it as "not given", and on a file sorted to 3 bytes the first reading searched an unsorted order.

| place | what 0 means there |
|---|---|
| `Header::sort_type`, `MaxQueryLen(0)` | sorted on whole suffixes; the format writes 0, and `Header::read` refuses a file with any other value |
| `OpenOptions::max_query_len`, `Some(0)` | since the sufr-106d02 fix, the same as `None` |
| `subsample_len`'s `Some(0)` arm | the same as `None`: group by the whole sort length |
| `searched_len`'s result, and `TypedSuffixArray::max_query_len` | compare the whole query |

`Header::sorted_len` turns the header's 0 into `text_len` for `subsample_len`, which is a fifth reading.

## Proposal

One spelling for "no cap" that is not a number, carried from the header struct to the search, so a reader never has to know which 0 this is. The file keeps writing 0, since the format is fixed, and `Header::read` and `write` are the one place that translate. Candidates: `Option<usize>` everywhere, or an enum `Cap { Whole, Bytes(usize) }` beside `SuffixSortType::Mask`. The decision is which, and whether `OpenOptions::max_query_len` then rejects `Some(0)` instead of accepting it as `None`.

notes.author: Jeb Rosen/8f73e884
notes.text:
Commit 52144cf, on branch `worktree-drop-sort-type` and not yet merged to dev, removes `SuffixSortType` and `searched_len`. That takes two rows out of the table:

- `Header::sort_type`'s `MaxQueryLen(0)` is now `Header::seed_mask()` returning `None`, so the header carries no 0 at all. The file still writes a zero-length mask.
- `searched_len` is gone. With every unmasked file sorted on whole suffixes it always returned `max_query_len.unwrap_or(0)`, and `open` now computes that directly.

`Header::sorted_len` returns `text_len` or the mask's weight with no 0 to translate. Still open: `TypedSuffixArray::max_query_len` stores 0 for "compare the whole query", and `OpenOptions::max_query_len` and `subsample_len` read `Some(0)` as `None`.
